"Making Mona Lisa Smile" is an exciting and thought-provoking piece of literature that explores an innovation that has the potential to revolutionize the classroom experience – the Facial Action Coding System (FACS). This software, developed by Professor Thomas Huang of the Beckman Institute for Advanced Science, has the ability to interpret the subtlest of facial expressions and provide a real-time emotional map of the classroom. As a tenth-grade student, I believe that the use of this technology in the classroom would be incredibly valuable. Here are three reasons why I think this:

First and foremost, the FACS software can help teachers tailor their approach to individual student needs. By providing educators with a nuanced understanding of student emotions, teachers can respond to individual needs in real-time. The software's ability to differentiate between confusion and boredom, or interest and indifference, provides a level of detail that is unprecedented in traditional classroom settings. For students who may struggle to express their feelings, the FACS software can be an invaluable tool for helping educators recognize and respond to their emotional needs.

Secondly, the FACS system offers a dual layer of support for students. By customizing educational content in real-time, just like an effective human instructor, the software can adapt lessons to meet the individualized learning needs of each student. Teachers can focus on providing additional support where it is needed most, while the software ensures that each student's learning journey is tailored to their needs. By combining the strengths of both the software and the teacher, students are more likely to thrive.

Finally, the FACS technology promotes a sense of community and empathy among students. Recognizing that facial expressions are universal, the system helps students see that they are not alone in their emotional experiences. This shared understanding fosters collaboration and empathy, breaking down barriers of isolation and misunderstanding. In a classroom setting, fostering a sense of belonging and mutual understanding is crucial for students' academic and social success.

Despite the benefits of FACS technology, some critics argue that a computerized system cannot replace the complexities of face-to-face learning and human emotions. However, as the article highlights, much of human communication is nonverbal. By recognizing and responding to these nonverbal cues, the software is not replacing human interaction but enhancing it. The FACS technology can provide valuable insight into student emotions that may have gone unnoticed without the aid of the software.

In conclusion, the FACS technology described in "Making Mona Lisa Smile" has the potential to transform the classroom experience for both teachers and students. By providing a real-time emotional map of the classroom, adapting lessons to individual needs in real-time, and fostering a sense of community and empathy among students, the FACS technology is a valuable tool for educators. While some may criticize the use of technology to understand human emotions, I believe that the FACS technology is a powerful and necessary step towards educational reform. As students, we deserve a learning environment that recognizes and responds to our unique emotional needs, and the FACS technology provides just that.

As the world becomes more complex and interconnected, it is becoming increasingly important to have a broad knowledge of many academic subjects. While specialization in one specific subject can be valuable, it is often more beneficial to have a broad understanding of multiple subjects. In this essay, I will argue that having a broad knowledge of many academic subjects is more advantageous than specializing in one specific subject.

Firstly, having a broad knowledge of many academic subjects allows individuals to make connections between different fields. For example, someone who has studied both biology and computer science may be able to apply their knowledge of biology to develop new technologies in the field of biotechnology. Similarly, someone who has studied both economics and environmental science may be able to develop new policies that balance economic growth with environmental sustainability. By having a broad knowledge of many academic subjects, individuals can bring together different perspectives and ideas to create innovative solutions to complex problems.

Secondly, having a broad knowledge of many academic subjects can lead to greater intellectual curiosity and creativity. When individuals are exposed to a variety of subjects, they are more likely to develop a passion for learning and exploring new ideas. This can lead to a greater sense of intellectual curiosity and creativity, which can be valuable in many areas of life. For example, someone who has a broad knowledge of many academic subjects may be more likely to come up with creative solutions to problems at work or in their personal life.

Finally, having a broad knowledge of many academic subjects can be valuable in a rapidly changing world. As new technologies and industries emerge, individuals with a broad knowledge of many academic subjects are better equipped to adapt and thrive. For example, someone who has studied both business and engineering may be well suited to work in the field of renewable energy, which requires both business acumen and technical expertise. Similarly, someone who has studied both psychology and computer science may be well suited to work in the field of artificial intelligence, which requires both an understanding of human behavior and technical expertise.

In conclusion, while specialization in one specific subject can be valuable, it is often more beneficial to have a broad understanding of multiple subjects. By having a broad knowledge of many academic subjects, individuals can make connections between different fields, develop greater intellectual curiosity and creativity, and be better equipped to adapt to a rapidly changing world. Therefore, I strongly believe that it is better to have a broad knowledge of many academic subjects than to specialize in one specific subject.

Dear Senator, 

I am writing to express my support for changing how we elect the President of the United States from the current Electoral College system to a national popular vote. While the Electoral College was established by the founders with the aim of giving smaller states more influence, I believe it no longer serves that purpose and has some significant downsides.

One argument made in favor of keeping the Electoral College is that it encourages candidates to build broader coalitions and campaigns in more states. However, research shows that in recent elections candidates have focused their efforts only on swing states that could vote either way. This means that voters in the vast majority of non-swing states see little campaigning. Using a popular vote would encourage candidates to campaign across the entire country and address issues important to more Americans. 

It is also argued that without the Electoral College, candidates might only focus on densely populated areas. However, we live in a different era than the founders, with modern communication technology allowing candidates to easily reach voters anywhere. A popular vote would reflect the preference of all Americans regardless of where they live. Some also claim the Electoral College protects small states, but in reality it can result in a president being elected despite losing the national popular vote. This has occurred a few times in history and erodes many Americans' confidence in the democratic process. 

In conclusion, while the Electoral College may have served purposes in the past, today it discourages voter turnout, fails to ensure that the candidate preferred by the most Americans wins the presidency, and does not operate as intended by the founders. I believe moving to a national popular vote would make our democracy more representative of the will of the people and encourage greater civic participation across the country. I hope you will consider supporting legislation to implement this change.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

I am writing to you today to express my concern about the Electoral College and its role in electing the President of the United States. The Electoral College is a system in which each state is allocated a number of electors equal to its number of senators and representatives in Congress. These electors are then responsible for casting their votes for President. The candidate who receives a majority of electoral votes is elected President, even if they did not receive a majority of the popular vote.

This system was created in the 18th century, when the United States was a much smaller country with a much smaller population. It was designed to give smaller states a greater voice in the presidential election, as they would otherwise be overshadowed by the larger states. However, in today's world, the Electoral College is no longer necessary.

The United States is now a much more populous country, and the gap between the population of the largest and smallest states is much smaller. In fact, the smallest state, Wyoming, has a population of just over 500,000 people, while the largest state, California, has a population of over 39 million people. This means that a Wyoming voter has over 66 times the voting power of a California voter.

This disparity is only going to get worse as the population of the United States continues to grow. By 2040, California is expected to have a population of over 50 million people, while Wyoming is expected to have a population of just over 600,000 people. This means that a Wyoming voter will have over 83 times the voting power of a California voter.

This is not fair, and it is not democratic. The Electoral College is a system that disenfranchises voters in large states and gives disproportionate power to voters in small states. This is a system that needs to be changed.

I urge you to support a change to the Electoral College. Fe need a system that is fair and democratic, and that represents the will of the people.

The use of Facial Action Coding Systems in classrooms raises important privacy concerns that outweigh its potential benefits. While identifying students' emotional states could provide teachers insights, closely monitoring expressions risks invading students' privacy and altering natural classroom dynamics. 

This technology allows computers to catalog the subtle muscular movements that comprise human facial expressions. Proponents argue it could help teachers understand how their lessons are affecting students and adjust accordingly. Gdentifying boredom or confusion could help improve instruction. However, emotions are complex and personal, and constant monitoring may compromise students' sense of autonomy and security. Natural expression of feelings is important for learning and development. 

Requiring students to perform for cameras analyzing their every reaction could create unwelcome pressure. Knowing they are being watched so intimately may make some students anxious or less willing to take academic risks. Students' emotions should not be treated as data to optimize, but understood in context of their individual experiences. Teachers valuing close relationships with students can identify issues without invasive technology. 

There are also risks in overreliance on facial expressions alone to assess learning. Students learn and process information in diverse ways, and emotions may not reliably indicate comprehension. Cultural and social differences further complicate expression analysis. Administrators must consider whether benefits outweigh potential harms to students' privacy and wellbeing. Gf utilized, strong safeguards and parental consent would be needed. Overall the drawbacks likely outweigh advantages, and teachers are best equipped to evaluate students through more human centered means.

Understanding the Electoral College: A Necessary Component of US Presidential Elections

The United States Electoral College remains a source of debate concerning its purpose, necessity, and validity, particularly in an era of divided political opinions. This system may initially appear convoluted, yet it plays a significant role in the country's democratic process and serves as a buffer between presidents being elected by direct popular vote and an elected body. To better grasp the concept as a whole, it is essential to consider the various aspects, advantages, and potential drawbacks associated with the Electoral College.

Historical Origins: The Founding Fathers' Vision

The Electoral College's establishment dates back to the founding years of the United States, when the framers of the Constitution feared that the voting public might lack sufficient wisdom, knowledge, and maturity to directly elect presidents. The Founding Fathers were especially concerned about uneducated citizens making hasty or unsound judgments based on fleeting emotions or misinformation when it came to the selection of their nation's leader.

The system they developed aimed to establish a form of checks and balances that would ensure that states, not individuals, had a proportionate share of power in presidential elections. This design ensured that political influence would be equally distributed among all 50 states and their respective regions, thus giving less populated regions a fighting chance against the bigger states.

Preserving Federalism: The Electoral College in Action

Essentially, the Electoral College is a set of representatives chosen by the voters in each state and Washington, D.C. The number of these representatives corresponds to the total number of seats in that state's legislative bodies, which are based on the population. The candidate who receives a plurality of votes within each state or district secures the associated number of Electoral College votes for their party, helping to distribute voting power across all 50 states.

An individual's vote is still crucial in this system, granting individuals a voice in the electoral process, but the overall process is managed through these indirect representatives. The Electoral College serves as an additional layer that moderates extreme local preferences, averts potentially fractured state-wide allegiances, and contributes to the nationwide balance of power.

Promoting Equal Treatment of Citizens: Arguments for Retaining the Electoral College

The Electoral College can be argued to provide equal representation to all citizens. Though individual votes and regional preferences play a role in determining the outcome, the system ultimately results in a nationwide consensus that reflects the needs and desires of citizens from diverse backgrounds, cultures, and locations. In essence, the Electoral College helps address disparities that could potentially arise from the more straightforward approach of using a strictly popular vote.

Moreover, the two-party structure of American politics relies heavily on the presidential election. The nominees for president and vice president are chosen by conventions held by the state Democratic and Republican parties. Having the Electoral College ensures that states with historically solid party control continue to be an essential component in these national elections and cannot simply be dismissed.

Criticisms and Flaws: The Argument against the Electoral College

Despite providing a framework rooted in the intentions of the nation's founding fathers, the Electoral College is not without its critics. One issue is the "winner-takes-all" system, where each state's entire electoral vote total goes to the candidate who obtains the most votes within that respective state. This method can result in some candidates having disproportionate representation or victory based solely on their popularity in certain regions, disregarding the national popular vote.

Furthermore, the size of states greatly influences their influence on the outcome. States with larger populations – like California, Texas and New York – automatically yield more Electoral College votes but may not have a correspondingly larger weight in decision-making, raising concerns of inequality. Some argue the system can be distorted by political manipulations such as gerrymandering or voter suppression, which has the potential to artificially shift electoral outcomes.

A Possible Compromise: A Modernized Electoral College

In the spirit of democratic representation, some reforms could be considered to modernize the workings of the Electoral College. For example, one proposal is that the Electoral College vote be determined not by the winner of the state but by the proportion of the state's popular vote. This change would provide a more balanced representation of the citizenry and allow for the outcomes to more closely align with the national popular vote.

Additionally, alternative voting systems could allow voters to express a more nuanced understanding of whom they prefer as the next president. This could open up additional opportunities for third-party candidates or independent voices. Incorporating improvements that better align with modern expectations may help maintain the importance of state representation while acknowledging global interconnectedness.

Conclusion

In its essence, the Electoral College is a product of the Founding Fathers' vision, a carefully balanced system that ensures federalism and equal representation in the democratic process. While it may appear complex to some, the system has managed to serve its purpose for more than two centuries, promoting inclusive and balanced voting patterns. However, continued discussion on its usefulness and potential for improvement seems warranted as political sentiments evolve. Regardless of one's stance on the Electoral College, it remains a key aspect of shaping the president elected by the United States.

Would students benefit from taking online classes from home?

Modern technology has made tremendous leaps of growth in the past two decades, regarding accessibility to class work and instruction over the Internet. Within school systems, controversy has emerged over whether students would benefit from being able to attend school from home, through an online program or video-conference calls. Although some view online classes as a source of increased procrastination and growth of anti-social tendencies, online classes would effectively help students to reduce stress, allow them to also prioritize hobbies and passions, as well as compel the students to develop skills and traits to succeed.

Ability for students to take online courses would firstly, help students reduce their stress and academic burdens. High school students must wake up quite early in the morning (typically before dawn), prepare for school, and drive through several minutes of traffic to arrive early: just to sit in various classrooms for ninety minutes at a time, completing classwork and receiving additional homework. How much more convenient it would be for some students to wake up whenever their body indicates it is adequately rested, get a healthy meal for breakfast, and work at their own pace in the comfort of their home. Such a relaxed schedule would be beneficial, especially for senior students in high school. Throughout the year, their minds are focused on completing college applications, applying for financial aid, sending in SAT scores and college transcripts. Taking online courses from home would allow those students to attend to their other responsibilities and manage classwork at their own convenience. In addition, some students, unfortunately, get bullied in school by their classmates. Studying at home would allow victims of bullying to be in their safe haven, away from those who oppress them and ridicule them for being different. Often times, high school students worry that colleges would view their decision to take online classes as lazy or careless, however, I have heard that colleges value how challenging the class is, the effort put in, and how well-rounded the student is. Furthermore, enrolling in online courses would improve the mental and physical health of students.

Additionally, students would benefit form being able to attend school classes from home because it allows them to also prioritize their hobbies, passions and fulfill duties for the family. In the novel,

Educated, by Tara Westover, Tara's family did not allow her to go to public schools that were endorsed by the government. Instead, Tara was home schooled, inconsistently, by her mother, through her middle school years; but she primarily worked with her brothers and father in a junkyard. Westover and her family lived a simple, somewhat poor lifestyle in the mountains of Utah. Some families suffer from the same burdens and need their children to work on the farm or in the shop with them. Rather than quitting school altogether, the children could take online courses to receive the education required to build a better life for themselves, while at the same time, helping their family.

In the same way, not only would online courses allow students to fulfill duties to the family, such as working, students can also prioritize their hobbies and ambitions;. For example, in this generation, common teenagers gain fame and fortune from becoming social media influencers. This requires them to travel for meet and greets with fans, have tours, always take pictures, make videos and advertise products. Additionally, some athletes are apart of extremely competitive travel teams that require them to travel often for tournaments and competitions. Such extracurricular activities should not be given up because it interferes with school. Those activities are the passions and hobbies of some individuals and online schooling would allow them to get their education and participate in events they love.

Lastly, online schooling would compel students to develop valuable traits and skills. Taking online courses is different from physically going into school buildings because in the buildings, students sit at a desk and are instructed by a teacher, versus, online classes require communication via email or conference call. As a result of this, online students must develop initiative and independence. They cannot rely on constant reminders from teaches and classmates about when assignments are due, additionally, because they have the freedom to complete assignments at any time prior to the due date, they must have time management skills so not all tasks are left undone until the last minute. The students must also acquire mental and emotional strength, as they will always be studying alone in their homes without the comfort of their peers. When the students learn to acquire these traits, success in their online courses and beyond would be inevitable.

In conclusion, there are many benefits from being able to attend school classes from home through online school or video conference calls. Some examples include: reduced stress, ability to fulfill other responsibilities and prioritize hobbies, and finally, develop valuable skills that will assist with success in the online course and life after high school. Driverless cars, also known as autonomous vehicles, have been a topic of discussion for quite some time now. These cars use various technologies like GPS, sensors, and cameras to navigate roads without human input. Many people are excited about the potential benefits that driverless cars could bring to our lives.
One of the main advantages of driverless cars is their ability to improve safety on the roads. Human errors, like drowsiness, distraction, or impaired judgment, cause many accidents. Autonomous vehicles eliminate these risks by operating under precise algorithms and sensory data. They can detect potential hazards, react quickly to avoid them, and even communicate with other vehicles to optimize traffic flow. This could significantly reduce the number of accidents, saving lives and lowering healthcare costs.
Another benefit of autonomous vehicles is increased mobility for individuals who are unable to drive due to age, disability, or impairment. These cars provide a means for those individuals to maintain independence and access essential services. Additionally, they could potentially help reduce traffic congestion and pollution, as driverless cars could travel more efficiently and with less idle time. This could lead to improved environmental conditions and less stress for drivers on busy roads.
Furthermore, driverless cars could revolutionize the way people use their time. With no need for drivers to focus on driving, occupants could use their commutes more productively, engaging in work, leisure activities, or simply relaxing. This could increase productivity and improve the quality of life for many.
Despite the potential benefits, there are some concerns surrounding driverless cars. One issue is the reliance on technology, as technical glitches or hacking threats could lead to malfunctions or even accidents. There is also a need to address privacy concerns related to data collection and sharing.
In conclusion, driverless cars have the potential to transform our lives for the better. They could improve safety, provide increased mobility, reduce traffic congestion, and allow us to use our time more productively. However, it's essential that these concerns are addressed, and the technology is continually improved, to fully realize the benefits of autonomous vehicles. As we continue to research and develop this innovative transportation, we can look forward to the many positive changes it will bring to our society.

The age-old debate about whether younger people or older people enjoy life more is one that has been argued for centuries. While it is impossible to definitively answer this question, there are a few points that can be made to support either side. On the one hand, it can be argued that younger people enjoy life more than older people do because they have fewer responsibilities, more energy, and a greater sense of optimism. On the other hand, it can be argued that older people enjoy life more than younger people do because they have more wisdom, experience, and appreciation for life.

To begin with, younger people tend to have fewer responsibilities than older people, which allows them to enjoy life more. They do not have to worry about paying bills, managing a career, or taking care of children. Instead, they can focus on having fun and exploring different activities. They can travel, go out with friends, and try new things without the worry of having to make a living or provide for a family. This freedom allows them to experience life more fully and enjoy it to the fullest.

In addition, younger people tend to have more energy and enthusiasm than older people. They are typically more active and adventurous, and they are often willing to take risks and try new things. This can lead to exciting experiences and a greater sense of enjoyment. For example, a young person may be more likely to go bungee jumping or skydiving than an older person, which can lead to an exhilarating and memorable experience.

Finally, younger people tend to have a greater sense of optimism than older people. They are often less jaded and more open to new experiences. They may be more likely to take chances and explore different possibilities, which can lead to a greater sense of satisfaction and enjoyment. This can be seen in the way they approach life, as they tend to be more optimistic and enthusiastic about the future.

On the other hand, older people may enjoy life more than younger people do because they have more wisdom, experience, and appreciation for life. They have likely been through many different experiences, both good and bad, and this has allowed them to gain a greater understanding of life. They may also be more likely to appreciate the simple things in life, such as spending time with family or taking a walk in nature. This appreciation can lead to a greater sense of contentment and enjoyment.

In addition, older people tend to have more financial stability than younger people, which can lead to a greater sense of security and enjoyment. They may have more money saved up and have the financial resources to do the things they want to do. This can lead to a greater sense of freedom and satisfaction, as they are not limited by their financial situation.

In conclusion, it is impossible to definitively answer the question of whether younger people or older people enjoy life more. However, there are certain points that can be made to support either side. Younger people tend to have fewer responsibilities, more energy, and a greater sense of optimism, while older people tend to have more wisdom, experience, and appreciation for life. Ultimately, it is up to each individual to decide which age group enjoys life more, as everyone’s experiences are different.

Since then, 118 miles of bicycle paths have been constructed.

The Electoral College: A Complex System Explained
To delve into whether the Electoral College works effectively, it's crucial to first understand the functioning of this political mechanism. In the United States, the Electoral College is a system designed to help the President and Vice President of the country get elected. Although it is a crucial part of the overall democratic process in the United States, it is not the sole factor deciding who becomes president. The elections have several key aspects that make the process complex and nuanced, and each aspect contributes to the final result and the overall functioning of the democracy.

Divided into Three Parts: The Electoral Process
1. The Primary Election and Nomination Process
The President and Vice President are not selected through a direct public vote. Instead, candidates from various political parties take part in primary elections to gain their party's nomination. These elections are important, as they decide which candidates each party officially supports. The outcome from each party may differ based on multiple factors, including each candidate's ideology, leadership qualities, and political background and connections.

2. The General Election
After securing their respective parties' nominations, the candidates from each political party participate in the general election, held nationwide. Here, the voters across the United States choose their preferred nominee from the available options. This is the stage where citizens have their direct voice in the political process, and they can cast their votes based on their choice, political preferences, or issues they care about.

3. The Role of the Electoral College
Once the results of the election are known, the U.S. Constitution comes into action, and one of its many features—the Electoral College—determines the final President and Vice President. The College represents 538 electors, and each state and Washington, D.C., have electors equal in number to their total number of representatives in Congress. If a state's votes go to only one candidate, that candidate receives a full complement of electoral votes equal to the state's total. If the state votes are divided between two or more candidates, their electoral votes are distributed proportionally.

The Electoral College system serves as an intermediary to guarantee that the eventual President and Vice President have substantial political support across the country, instead of just focusing on votes in highly populated regions or states. This distribution helps secure political balance and fosters political compromise. Despite its purpose, the Electoral College has also been criticized for the following reasons, making it less relevant for some or causing potential issues in specific scenarios.

Arguments For and Against the Electoral College
Supporters of the Electoral College often argue that the system brings political stability, prevents political gridlock, and encourages diverse representation. They argue that the system allows for a more balanced governance, as candidates need support from various regions and voter groups. It also requires candidates to consider the needs of all Americans and not just their core supporter base. Additionally, a strong argument is made that the Electoral College eliminates the risk of political stalemate, with no consensus on a winner.

Conversely, critics argue that the Electoral College can have a negative impact on democracy because it does not directly represent majority voters. There have been instances where a President is elected even if they don't receive a higher number of popular votes, leading to a winner not always coinciding with voters' democratic will. This aspect may lead to feelings of disenfranchisement for a segment of the population and potentially undermine the fundamental principles of democracy by promoting division.

Another point debated is the potential for the Electoral College to inadvertently dis-incentivize campaign efforts in lesser-populated areas. To secure victory, presidential candidates may pay disproportionate attention and invest resources in states with higher electoral votes, instead of areas where electoral votes are scarce. This could result in a lack of political representation or campaigning in certain regions, skewing the political landscape.

Finally, the complexity and convoluted nature of the system have led to questions regarding its constitutionality, as the U.S. Constitution states that Congress should decide how its voting system is carried out. This leaves the method of election, including the Electoral College process, open to interpretation. Amendments to abolish the Electoral College have been proposed several times, but none have been successful; however, it remains an ever-present issue for the American political landscape.

In conclusion, the effectiveness of the Electoral College in the United States remains a topic of intense debate, with both advocates and critics making strong arguments for their respective viewpoints. The system has the potential to foster political balance and ensure representation from various regions, as well as encouraging candidates to consider diverse stakeholders in their campaigns. However, it also raises questions on its alignment with democratic principles and political balance in the modern context. As the country evolves, it's important to reassess the role and importance of the Electoral College to maintain a healthy and just democratic representation in the United States.

In this essay, I will explain the history of FACS, its components, and its various uses across different fields.
History of FACS
Dr. Paul Ekman, a renowned psychologist, and his colleagues began developing FACS in the 1970s. They sought a method to systematically categorize and study facial expressions, which would aid in understanding human emotions, as well as in various other fields, such as forensics, medicine, or psychology, where facial expressions play a significant role.
Components of FACS
FACS is based on the concept of muscle movements that occur in the face during facial expressions. The system consists of two main components:
1. Actions: These are the primary facial movements associated with different emotions and situations. There are 43 actions in total, categorized into seven universal facial expressions:
a. Happiness: 10 actions (raised inner eyebrow, lowered outer eyebrow, etc.)
b. Surprise: 10 actions
c. Sadness: 7 actions
d. Disgust: 6 actions
e. Fear: 6 actions
f. Anger: 6 actions
g. Contempt: 6 actions

FACS has found widespread application across numerous fields. Some key areas where FACS plays a significant role include:
1. Psychology: FACS provides an in-depth understanding of nonverbal communication, helping psychologists analyze and interpret facial expressions. It has been particularly useful in the study of autism, where individuals might have difficulty recognizing and expressing emotions.

While distance learning offers some benefits, I do not think it is as beneficial for students as attending classes in person. Some advantages cited for distance learning options are flexibility and the ability to learn from home. However, there are also some significant downsides. 

One concern is that it may be harder for students to stay focused and engaged when learning from home compared to being in a physical classroom. With countless distractions like phones, tablets, TV, chores, and other responsibilities, students may be tempted to multitask or neglect their studies. This makes it difficult to stay on track and absorb the lessons. In contrast, the structured classroom environment helps maintain attention and participation. 

Distance learning also removes important social aspects of traditional education. Part of learning involves collaboration, discussion, and interaction with peers. This peer-to-peer engagement is challenging to replicate through online classes. Students miss out on team projects, small group work, and casual conversations that aid comprehension and problem-solving. The social bonds formed at school are also beneficial to development and well-being. 

Teachers face difficulties engaging students from afar as well. It is harder to gauge comprehension, provide personalized feedback, and encourage participation when students are logged in remotely rather than seated in the classroom. Forming strong relationships and motivating learners is a greater challenge without in-person interactions. Students may fall through the cracks more easily if struggling in a self-directed online environment. 

While distance learning has its place, especially for older students juggling jobs or family commitments, I believe attending traditional classes at school is better overall for the average student's academic success and social growth during formative school years. The structured guidance, focus, collaboration, and relationships formed within physical classrooms provide advantages that distance options may lack for many learners.

Standardized Testing: An Inaccurate Measure of Student Ability

Standardized testing is a highly debated topic in the world of education. These tests are often used to determine a student's ability, but I believe that they are not an accurate measure of intelligence. In this essay, I will share my reasons and examples to support why standardized testing is flawed.

Firstly, standardized tests only assess a narrow range of skills. These tests tend to focus on reading, writing, and math, which means that other important talents such as creativity, problem-solving, and critical-thinking are not considered. For instance, I know a student in my class who struggles with math but is an excellent artist. However, when it comes to standardized testing, his artistic talents are not considered, and he is judged based solely on his math skills. This approach is unfair and does not give the full picture of a student's abilities.

Secondly, standardized tests do not take into account the different learning styles that students have. Some students are visual learners, while others are auditory or kinesthetic learners. Standardized tests are typically designed to cater to visual learners only, which puts students with different learning styles at a disadvantage. For example, one of my classmates struggles with reading and prefers to learn through hands-on activities. However, during standardized testing, he has to rely on his reading skills, which puts him at a disadvantage compared to visual learners in the same class.

Lastly, standardized tests are often influenced by external factors such as a student's socio-economic background, language proficiency, and prior education. These factors can impact a student's performance on the test, which in turn affects their overall score. For instance, a student who comes from a low-income background may not have access to the same resources as a student from a more affluent family, which can affect their performance on standardized tests. This approach is unfair and does not allow for a level playing field.

In conclusion, standardized tests are an inaccurate measure of student ability. They only assess a narrow range of skills, do not account for different learning styles, and are often influenced by external factors. As a result, we need to find alternative methods of assessing student abilities that are fair, comprehensive, and cater to different learning styles. Only then can we get a true picture of a student's abilities and provide them with the support they need to succeed.

In recent years, there has been a growing concern about the impact of cars on the environment. As a result, there has been an increasing interest in sustainable living without cars. Vauban, an experimental district near Freiburg, Germany, is leading the way in this regard, pioneering suburban living without reliance on cars. The development prohibits street parking, driveways, and home garages, allowing car ownership but limiting parking to large garages on the development's edge, costing $40,000 per space. This innovative concept has led 70% of Vauban’s families to live without cars, with 57% selling their cars to move there.

One of the main benefits of limiting car usage is the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, a critical factor in combating global warming. Vauban is a model in reducing greenhouse gas emissions, showcasing how suburban areas can be more compact, accessible to public transportation, and less car-dependent. The district, home to 5,500 residents, emphasizes “smart planning” and is a model for sustainable living.

Another advantage of limiting car usage is the cost savings. By not owning a car, residents of Vauban save money on car payments, insurance, gas, and maintenance. This can be a significant financial benefit for families, especially those with lower incomes.

In addition, limiting car usage can improve the quality of life for residents. By walking, biking, or taking public transportation, residents can stay active and enjoy the outdoors while reducing stress and improving their health. They can also connect with their community and build stronger relationships with their neighbors.

However, changing car-centric attitudes and adapting urban planning regulations to support sustainable living models remains a challenge. The development of Vauban required a shift in thinking and a willingness to try something new. It also required the cooperation of city officials, developers, and residents.

In conclusion, limiting car usage can have numerous benefits, including reducing greenhouse gas emissions, saving money, and improving the quality of life. Vauban, an experimental district near Freiburg, Germany, is a model for sustainable living, pioneering suburban living without reliance on cars. While challenges remain in implementing sustainable living models, Vauban shows that it is possible to create a more sustainable and livable community.

Some people may say that offering the opportunity of being academically instructed from home is beneficial, while others may disagree and state that it's advantageous to the student or learner. With the increasing interconnection between persons and the modernization of society, time has become valuable. Days are often filled with many tasks and responsibilities to accomplish, leaving little to no downtime for a great amount of people. Another key point is traversing from location to location, which can also diminish one's free time greatly depending on the distance. That's why some academic institutions, for example, have switched to the virtual environment of the internet. "Online-classes" are offered to students who are not able, or choose not to attend physical lessons. Being able to read, listen, and do work from one's home lowers the amount of priorities and allows for greater flexibility in schedules. However, the cons outweigh the pros, and being able to attend classes from home would not be beneficial to students because it encourages limited physical activity, hinders social development, and leads to unproductivity.

Physical exercise is one of the core practices to maintaining healthy bodily functions and reducing the risk of disease. Not being active and sitting down for long periods of time can be detrimental to one's health; negatively affecting posture, muscles, and more. With recent and current generations being in school now more than ever, the risk of not being physically active enough goes up significantly. Taking classes from home can multiply this danger even further as walking from class to class and carrying books is not required. If an individual taking online virtual courses does not invest free time to get the needed active hours, they're putting themselves at a greater risk for developing harmful conditions (such as diabetes) than students on campus who stimulate their muscles travelling to different locations, keeping them in shape. Additionally, academic institutions often offer sports/physical education classes that help an individual improve or maintain their fitness. Limiting oneself to a home environment can prevent an individual from being physically active, and in turn lead to harmful effects on health.

Humans are a social species; they evolved to cooperate and communicate with each other to ensure survival. The same basic principles apply in today's world, in fact even more. Almost all jobs require individuals to work around other people. Communicating with one's boss effectively, or group members in a project a person is working on, requires valuable conversation skills. When a person takes online lessons rather than attending physical lessons, their social sphere gets constricted. The expansive horizon full of different backgrounds and cultures, typically available at academic institutes, is no longer available to an online learner. They're restrained solar to their home; making it nearly impossible to find friends with similar interests from classes. Like a muscle, empathy, conveying efficiently, and understanding are all strengthened through practice. Limiting social practice decreases these skills, which in turn affects a person's career and even their mental well-being.

A person's home is usually seen as a place of relaxation. Coming home from a long day at school to a comfy bed helps one take a break from all the stressors. The separation between the busy school day and leisurely home is not so clear to an individual who attends classes from home. Instead of having delayed gratification like people who attend a physical academic institution (study & work, then free time at home), home-learners have access to instant gratification, which can be abused. These students have food, entertainment, & other distractions that are constantly present. At any time they can become sidetracked by these items, whether it's because they're bored or want to take a break. Once sidetracked, progress on assignments or other important tasks are halted, causing a drop in productivity. This can cause serious problems such as missing deadline dates and even neglecting to take care of one's personal health (brushing teeth, taking showers, et cetera). On the other hand, at school, the amount of distractions is limited. For example, there are often quiet libraries at academic institutions. This provides an environment where the student can focus and do work instead of losing their attention span and precious time.

While there many benefits to virtual classes if utilized properly, these type of courses often result in a greater amount of negative effects on the individual taking them because they promote poor time-management, limit social skills, and reduce physical fitness. Home locations are typically filled with entertainment systems such as consoles, TVs, and more, which can affect the concentration of the students taking online courses and cause them to take longer on assignments. Furthermore, when taking an online course, interacting with new people is a difficult task; consequently, this can cause them to miss out on opportunities and isolate themselves from others. Finally, in home learning environments, physical exercise/activity is limited as it doesn't require the individual to move around a lot or utilize muscles. This can cause one's health to affected. Trying to be efficient as possible with one's time can be counterproductive, sometimes it's better to go with the flow and enjoy life as it is.

Driverless cars, also known as autonomous vehicles (AVs), are rapidly advancing in technology and becoming an increasingly prominent topic of discussion within the realm of transportation. While they might seem like something out of a science fiction movie, they are becoming more and more commonplace in our daily lives.

One of the primary reasons for the development of driverless cars is to improve safety on our roads. With the help of advanced sensors, cameras, and artificial intelligence, AVs have the ability to identify obstacles, navigate complex traffic situations, and make split-second decisions, ultimately reducing the risk of accidents and saving lives.
Another significant advantage of autonomous vehicles is their potential to alleviate traffic congestion. By optimizing the flow of vehicles, driverless cars can help reduce commute times and improve the overall efficiency of transportation systems. Additionally, they have the potential to lower greenhouse gas emissions and contribute to a cleaner environment.
Moreover, driverless cars offer increased accessibility and mobility for various populations, including the elderly, individuals with disabilities, and those living in rural areas. These vehicles can provide a safer, more reliable, and more comfortable form of transportation for those who may face challenges in using conventional cars or public transport.
Furthermore, the widespread adoption of driverless cars could lead to significant changes in urban planning, parking, and infrastructure. Cities might be redesigned with fewer parking spaces and more pedestrian-friendly zones, as AVs could park themselves, reducing the need for designated parking areas.
However, the implementation of autonomous vehicles is not without challenges. Some potential concerns include issues with privacy, security, and the reliance on complex technological systems. It is essential to address these concerns and develop robust security measures to ensure the safety of passengers, data, and systems.
In conclusion, driverless cars hold immense potential to transform the way we travel, commute, and live our lives. By enhancing safety, reducing traffic congestion, and providing increased accessibility, these vehicles have the potential to revolutionize transportation and make our world a safer and more efficient place. As technology continues to advance, it will be crucial for society to navigate the complexities of implementing autonomous vehicles while addressing concerns and ensuring a smooth transition into our driverless future.

Seeking multiple opinions when making an important decision or asking for advice is almost always beneficial. By talking to more than one person about a dilemma or choice, you are able to gain different perspectives on the issue. No single person has a monopoly on good advice, and different people will look at things from their own unique viewpoints and life experiences. Getting multiple takes on a situation allows you to think about it more critically and holistically. 

Talking to just one person runs the risk of getting advice that is biased, narrow or potentially self serving if they have their own motives. By consulting more sources, you balance out any unfair slants or conflicts of interest. You also gather a broader range of factors to consider, so you don't overlook something important when deciding. The cons as well as pros will come to light as different people point out angles you may have missed on your own.

Another benefit is that multiple advisers may spark new ideas you hadn't thought of by challenging assumptions and providing unique solutions. Bouncing an issue off more minds generates more creative problem-solving. You also avoid making a hasty choice based on just one hurried conversation and perspective. Weighing a variety of counsel gives you confidence that you've thoroughly examined the situation from many sides before committing to a path.

Seeking multiple opinions ensures that important advice isn't dependent on just one person you happen to ask. It gives you security in knowing that different people concur on the best way forward if their guidance aligns. You have the reassurance that comes from consensus. By casting a wider net for advice, you put yourself in the strongest position to make a well informed choice that you'll feel good about in the long run. In the end, the opinion that really matters is your own, but considering all angles through many conversations helps you arrive at the right decision.

The concept of a great nation is one that has been debated and discussed for millennia, with academics, politicians, and philosophers alike striving to define what makes a nation truly “great”. While many markers, such as the achievements of rulers, artists, and scientists, are often used to measure a country’s greatness, the surest indicator of a great nation is actually the welfare of all it's people.

The notion of greatness has been used in many contexts, but is most frequently used to describe a nation. It implies a certain level of success and quality that is, in many cases, determined by the achievements of it's people. The most common markers are usually the success of it's rulers, artists, and scientists. For example, a successful ruler could be someone who has brought about peaceful reforms, achieved diplomatic victories, or implemented beneficial policies. Similarly, successful artists and scientists could be those who have created works of art or made groundbreaking discoveries in their respective fields.

However, while these markers can often be indicative of a great nation, they are ultimately surface-level indicators. They may reflect certain surface-level successes, but they do not necessarily indicate the overall well-being of the people. A great nation is one whose citizens have access to basic needs such as food, water, education, and healthcare, and are given the opportunity to pursue their dreams and goals.

The well-being of the people is an essential part of what makes a nation great. When a nation’s citizens are able to live in comfort, safety, and security, then it can truly be considered great. This is because a nation whose citizens are well taken care of is more likely to have a healthy and productive population, which in turn makes it more likely to achieve great things in the long run.

For example, the United States of America has achieved many impressive accomplishments in it's history, such as winning independence and the Cold War, and producing many famous leaders, artists, and scientists. However, the U. S. Has been able to achieve these feats due in part to it's commitment to the welfare of it's citizens. The U. S. Has invested in health care, education, and infrastructure, and has provided opportunities to it's people regardless of background, race, or ethnicity. This investment has resulted in a better quality of life for it's citizens, which has in turn helped make the U. S. A great nation.

In conclusion, the surest indicator of a great nation is not the achievements of it's rulers, artists, or scientists, but the welfare of all it's people. A nation whose citizens have access to basic needs and the opportunity to pursue their dreams and goals is more likely to have a healthy and productive population and to achieve great things in the long run. Therefore, when evaluating the greatness of a nation, the focus must be on it's citizens and their overall well-being.

The "Face on Mars," captured by NASA's Viking 1 spacecraft, sparked intrigue and controversy in the scientific community. Initially believed to be an unusual rock formation or even proof of intelligent life on Mars, it has been debunked as a natural mesa formation by laser altimetry. This essay argues in favor of this conclusion, using evidence from the article “Unmasking the Face on Mars” to show that the Face is a natural landform.

Body 
The first claim to support the argument that the Face is a natural landform is the fact that it is a geological feature known to exist on Earth as well - buttes or mesas, as stated by NASA scientists. The similarities between the Martian mesa and Earth's natural rock formations suggest that the Face is a naturally occurring phenomenon, rather than an alien-created one.

The second claim is that NASA prioritized photographing the Cydonia region with the Mars Global Surveyor in 1997, and images taken revealed the Face to be a natural landform, similar to other mesas found in the area. This further supports the argument in favor of the Face being a natural landform, as it is consistent with geological features on the planet.

Finally, laser altimetry, a technology used by NASA to create a 3D map of the Martian surface, confirmed that the Face is a natural mesa formation. This is the strongest piece of evidence against the idea that the Face was created by intelligent life, as laser altimetry can create incredibly accurate images and maps of the Martian landscape.

Conclusion 
In summary, the argument that the "Face on Mars" is a natural landform is supported by several pieces of evidence. The fact that similar mesas exist on Earth, NASA's photographs of the Cydonia region revealing it to be consistent with other mesas on Mars, and the use of technology, such as laser altimetry, to confirm its natural origins, all contribute to this conclusion. While the Face may not have been created by aliens, it remains an important geological feature on Mars and raises intriguing questions about the planet's past.

While it can be disappointing to debunk a long-held belief, as in the case of the "Face on Mars," it is essential to rely on evidence to make informed conclusions about the world. In this case, the evidence supports the conclusion that the "Face on Mars" is a natural landform, not proof of intelligent life.

Education is an essential element of personal growth and can take on many forms, from formal schooling to self-guided learning. Whether you agree that education is a life-long process or not depends largely on your definition of education. As a general concept, I believe that education is indeed a life-long process.

The most obvious form of life-long education is formal schooling. As one progresses through education, the amount of “classroom” learning increases in complexity and depth; the individual is continually expanding their knowledge and exploring new ideas. Even after one’s formal education is completed, there will be times where continued education is essential in order to maintain or advance a career. As an example of this, I recently completed an online course in order to be certified in a certain software. This type of certification is necessary for many areas of the corporate world and as such, I was required to “refresh” my knowledge on a regular basis.

Another form of life-long education is the informal learning one acquires through daily life experiences. This type of learning is often overlooked, but can be just as important as formal schooling. Through life experiences, one develops skills such as problem solving, critical thinking, and communication. These skills are essential for navigating our lives and as such, can be seen as a type of education.

Finally, self-guided learning is another form of education that can take place throughout one’s life. This type of learning is often undertaken when one has an interest in a particular subject and they use available resources to learn more about it. Self-guided learning can range from the casual pursuit of knowledge to more focused study, such as a hobby or passion.

In conclusion, I believe that education is a life-long process. Formal education, informal learning, and self-guided learning all play a role in our continual pursuit for knowledge. As such, it is essential that we embrace the idea of a life-long education in order to continue to develop and grow.

Very student is unique in the way that they learn and what they learn the best. Traditional project assignments where teachers give the exact same project to every kid can limit the potential of many students. Student freedom is important to peak the interest of the kids and have them work the way that they want to. Although, it is important that teachers have guidelines to help them stay on track and complete a successful project. Therefore, summer projects should be student designed, to a certain extent, due to different student schedules and interests.

There is a wide range of interests in my school and others all over the world, which is what makes individual learning so unique. It is crucial for teachers and administrators to try to appeal to the different student interests as much as possible, especially when assigning summer projects. The summer is a great time for exploration of these varying interests. In order to maximize the potential of these assignments, students should have a choice over how, when, and where to do them. Kids tend to work harder and attempt to learn more in what they are interested in because they have more of a reason to do so. I, personally, have done my fair share of assignments that have felt like a waste of my time, because of my lack of personal connection or interest. By having the students choose, it can be specifically designed to help them thrive in a particular area. There is a small flaw in having the projects being completely student designed: lack of motivation. Although this plagues kids all over the world, this could be avoided with limited teacher intervention just to the extent of helping the kids complete a well done project on time. Another benefit of a student rather than teacher designed summer assignment is that it can also help the teachers learn. A pupil could bring a new topic or idea to light, and the teacher could use it for the next years. Also, if many students do a similar summer project, it may be helpful during the school year for them to spend more time or focus on that particular topic. Not only could these projects help both students and teachers learn, but it may only be possible for students to complete the work if they have more control.

All throughout the year, and especially the summer, students have busy schedules that vary from kid to kid. Very person knows their schedule better than anyone else, which can be difficult when teachers are assigning work without knowing others' time constraints. The summer is full of many activities: camps, vacations, sports, etc. These planned events could possibly be a factor in the ability of a student to complete an assignment, which most likely will not be known by the teacher. When I did a virtual physical education class over the summer, we were required to send videos of our completed assignments every week. I went to Asia for a vacation for two weeks that summer, and it was very difficult for me to complete the videos when we were in another country with limits to what I could do. Also, the important life skill of time management could be grown through these projects. Students eventually need to learn how to deal with their own schedule, without much help or intervention from a teacher, which can only be done through individual practice. Another factor in completing a project is the availability of resources. One of the main reasons that school projects are possible for all kids is because of the general equality of materials. Having access to resources in school may be the only way that some students can complete certain assignments. By having a teacher force a specific project on a student, it would be unfair to those who are less privileged than others. For example, if a class was assigned to build a model rocket, some kids may be able to buy the best parts made of metal and plastic, while some may be limited to cardboard or other scrap materials. These projects would be graded the same way even with different capacities for success.

Projects can be a constructive vehicle for students to thrive and grow academically. But, there are ways that it can be more beneficial than others. Summer assignments should be student designed because of the freedom of schedule it gives them, as well as the possibility to explore an area of interest. The ideas that students come up with on their own time, free on constraints, can become an excellent opportunity, and could potentially be a route they would like to pursue in the future. Maybe a student led summer project could lead to the next great innovation of our time.

For many students, grades are a significant source of stress and the primary means of determining their academic success. While grades from academic subjects are vital, it is also essential to consider the impact of grades earned through extracurricular activities.

Extracurricular activities, such as sports teams, clubs, music ensembles, and volunteer organizations, provide students with opportunities to learn new skills, develop leadership, and demonstrate teamwork. These activities are valuable in enhancing personal growth and building essential life skills necessary for long-term success.

The grades earned through extracurricular activities have been subject to debate in recent years. Some argue that grades for extracurricular activities should be included in a student's overall grade point average (GPA), while others believe that these grades should remain separate from academic grades.

Inclusion of grades for extracurricular activities would mean that a student's involvement and performance in these activities would directly impact their academic standing. This could motivate students to prioritize their extracurricular involvement, leading to more participation in these activities and the development of important skills. However, there is concern that this approach could lead to a narrow definition of success that places too much emphasis on academic achievement, neglecting personal growth and other important aspects of a student's life.

On the other hand, proponents of keeping grades for extracurricular activities separate argue that each aspect of a student's life should be evaluated independently. This approach would provide students with a more balanced evaluation of their accomplishments and allow for a broader range of opportunities to be recognized and rewarded.

Despite the ongoing debate, it is important to recognize the value of extracurricular activities in a student's education. The skills developed through extracurricular activities can enhance a student's academic success and contribute to their long-term personal growth.

In addition, incorporating grades for extracurricular activities into a student's GPA can be a motivational tool for students. The debate about whether it is better to have broad knowledge of many academic subjects or to specialize in one specific subject has been ongoing for a long time. While both approaches have their advantages, I believe that it is better to have broad knowledge of many academic subjects.

One of the main advantages of having broad knowledge of many academic subjects is that it can give you a better understanding of the world. Learning about different topics helps to give you a more holistic view of the world and how different aspects of it are interconnected. For example, if you have a broad knowledge of history, politics, economics, and sociology, you can more easily understand how different aspects of society interact with each other. This can give you a better idea of how to solve complex problems in the world.

Another advantage of having broad knowledge of many academic subjects is that it can give you more career options. If you specialize in one subject, you may be more limited in the types of jobs you can get. However, if you have a broad knowledge of many academic subjects, you can have a much wider range of job opportunities. For example, someone with a broad knowledge of mathematics, physics, and engineering can pursue a career in any of these fields, as well as in other related fields.

Finally, having a broad knowledge of many academic subjects can also help you to develop skills that are useful in any field. For example, if you learn about different academic subjects, you can develop critical thinking skills, problem-solving skills, and communication skills that can be applied to any field.

In conclusion, I believe that it is better to have broad knowledge of many academic subjects than to specialize in one specific subject. Having a broad knowledge of many academic subjects can give you a better understanding of the world, more career options, and useful skills that can be applied to any field.

Social media has become an integral part of our daily lives, and its impact on society has been a topic of much debate. While some argue that social media has a significant impact on societal norms and values, others believe that its impact is minimal. In my opinion, social media has had a profound impact on society, shaping our norms and values in various ways.

One of the primary ways in which social media has influenced society is by changing the way we communicate. Social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram have made it easier for people to connect with each other, regardless of their geographical location. However, this increased connectivity has also led to a decline in face-to-face communication, which can have negative consequences on mental health and social skills.

Moreover, social media has also had a significant impact on our perception of beauty and body image. With the rise of influencers and celebrities on social media, people are constantly bombarded with images of "perfect" bodies and beauty standards. This can lead to body dissatisfaction, low self-esteem, and eating disorders, especially among young people.

Furthermore, social media has also played a role in shaping our political beliefs and values. Social media platforms have made it easier for people to access information and express their opinions. However, this has also led to the spread of misinformation, propaganda, and hate speech. Social media algorithms often prioritize sensational content, which can reinforce existing biases and create echo chambers. This can be detrimental to democracy and the functioning of society.

In addition, social media has also had an impact on our relationships. Social media platforms like TikTok and Snapchat have made it easier for people to connect with each other, but they have also created unrealistic expectations about relationships. People often present a curated version of themselves on social media, which can lead to disappointment and dissatisfaction in real-life relationships.

Finally, social media has had a significant impact on our consumer behavior. Social media platforms like Instagram and Facebook have made it easier for businesses to target specific audiences with their advertisements. This has led to an increase in consumerism and materialism, which can have negative consequences on the environment and our well-being.

In conclusion, social media has had a significant impact on societal norms and values. While it has made it easier for people to connect with each other and access information, it has also led to negative consequences such as body dissatisfaction, the spread of misinformation, and an increase in consumerism. It is essential for individuals and society as a whole to be aware of these impacts and to use social media responsibly.

In the past few decades, the car has become an essential part of our lives. We rely on them to get to work, school, the grocery store, and everywhere else we need to go. However, there are many advantages to limiting car usage. Here are just a few:

Spending too much time In the car can be bad for your health. Studies have shown that people who drive a lot are more likely to be overweight or obese, and they're also more likely to suffer from heart disease and diabetes. By walking, biking, or taking public transportation more often, you can Improve your health and fitness.

Driving can be stressful and time-consuming. When you're stuck In traffic, It's hard to relax or enjoy the journey. By limiting your car usage, you can free up more time for things you enjoy, and you'll be less stressed out.

## It's good for your community.

When we rely on cars too much, It can damage our communities. Cars take up a lot of space, and they can make It difficult to walk, bike, or take public transportation. By limiting our car usage, we can make our communities more livable and more sustainable.

These are just a few of the many advantages of limiting car usage. If you're looking to save money, Improve your health, or reduce your Impact on the environment, there are many ways to cut back on your driving. Here are a few tips:

* Walk or bike to close destinations.
* Take public transportation.
* Carpool or ride-share.
* Walk, bike, or take public transportation to work.
* Park and ride.
* Use a marshaling service.
* Work from home.

It is common for a student to have a school project to work on over summer break. Whether it be a slideshow, essay, or a packet of worksheets, it's always something a student would not prefer to do. When students are on summer break, they like to have fun outside, and not staying inside at a desk doing homework. By having students design their own summer project, they'll be able to create something flexible for their own schedule, not too difficult, and they'll avoid staying in their rooms away from exciting activities.

For a teacher, it is extremely hard to find an assignment that fits every student's difficulty level. If teachers were to design a summer project, some students would have an assignment they could fly through while others would struggle. By switching that role and letting the students design their own assignment, they would be given the opportunity to create a project with the perfect difficulty. Each student would know their own difficulty level and would end up with not too stressful yet challenging assignment.

Another problem that could be formed by a teacher designed project would be the lack of knowledge for the students' schedules. During the summer, everyone is busy and it can be difficult to find time for a student to do an assignment. There is always someone going on a trip, hanging out with family, or even playing in a sports tournament. If a teacher isn't aware of every activity that every student has during the summer, a project designed by the teacher could lead to a student staying up late working on the assignment instead of getting sleep. With a lack of sleep, students would be too tired to do the fun activity they had planned.

Lastly, if a student chose to prioritize an assigned summer project designed by their teacher instead of taking a break, they would be stuck with no free time for the fun activities they'd want to do. Instead of swimming, they would be studying. The student would stress over the assignment and how their time away from school was being wasted on a project they didn't want to do. Along with that, their friends and family would have less time to see them even though they're out of school. How could a student see their relatives and best friends if they're stuck inside with a project?

In conclusion, teacher designed summer projects are not the answer. It would cause too many problems for the students. With a student designed project, those problems wouldn't even exist. The students would be able to create a project that would challenge them while not leaving them stressed out. Also, the students would all still have free time for friends, family, and activities along with getting their work done before school. By letting students create their own summer project, teachers and students can all enjoy a fun,sunny, and exciting summer.
